subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on all legacy ownerless session rows, with recovery limited to operators or non-plugin clients?
rationale: Rejecting ownerless rows prevents unsafe plugin adoption, but it is an upgrade-visible restriction that can stop previously working plugin patch flows and has no safe automatic ownership migration.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Reject ownerless plugin-runtime patches, document the operator recovery path, and require live upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Define a provenance migration
options.body: Add a doctor-owned migration only for rows whose original plugin ownership can be established safely and deterministically.

options.title: Preserve temporary compatibility
options.body: Allow ownerless rows through a narrowly defined temporary compatibility rule with explicit security limits and a removal plan.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless plugin-runtime patches, document the operator recovery path, and require live upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest involvement in gateway session mutation, storage migration, and lifecycle policy boundaries.
